original_text:
Resolution v.Magnification
–Resolution:•The ability to distinguish two points which are closely adjacent and would otherwise appear to be one.•“Higher” (better) resolution is a shorter distance; “lower” (poorer) resolution is a longer distance
–Magnification:•The degree of enlargement of an image as compared to the original.•A measure of the increase in diameter of a structure.•Written as a quantity X (ex: 1000X) for                                                   how many times the image is magnified
explanation: This slide distinguishes between resolution and magnification. Resolution is the ability to distinguish two points that are closely adjacent and would otherwise appear as a single point. A 'higher' (better) resolution corresponds to a shorter distance of separation, whereas a 'lower' (poorer) resolution represents a longer distance. Magnification is defined as the degree of enlargement of an image compared to the original, which measures the increase in the diameter of a structure. It is expressed as a number followed by an X (e.g., 1000X) representing how many times the image has been enlarged.

questions.q: What is the definition of resolution in microscopy?
opts: The degree of enlargement of an image compared to the original
The ability to distinguish two closely adjacent points that would otherwise appear as one
The distance from the lens where passing rays converge
The process of staining a specimen to make it visible
questions.exp: The slide defines resolution as: 'The ability to distinguish two points which are closely adjacent and would otherwise appear to be one.'

questions.q: How is magnification measured and written?
opts: As a wavelength value in nanometers
As a quantity X (e.g., 1000X) representing the increase in diameter of a structure compared to the original
As a ratio of pixels on a digital screen
questions.exp: The text states magnification is: 'A measure of the increase in diameter of a structure. Written as a quantity X (ex: 1000X) for how many times the image is magnified'.
